sentences.en: Welcome to The Rest is History with me, Dominic Sandbrook, and my psychic, or my puppet master as he calls himself, Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听由我——多米尼克·桑德布鲁克，以及我的灵媒（或者像他自己说的那样，我的幕后操纵者）汤姆·霍兰共同主持的《一切皆历史》。

sentences.en: Tom, hello.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你好。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Happy New Year.
sentences.zh: 新年快乐。

sentences.en: Happy New Year.
sentences.zh: 新年快乐。

sentences.en: Now, we are not yet in the New Year.
sentences.zh: 话说回来，我们现在其实还没到新年。

sentences.en: We're anticipating the New Year.
sentences.zh: 我们是在展望新年。

sentences.en: So, we are very exercised, aren't we, about the B word, the word that's been on everybody's lips for the last five years or so, Brexit.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们对那个“B”打头的词非常热心，不是吗？就是过去五年左右一直挂在每个人嘴边的那个词——脱欧。

sentences.en: And we don't know what's going to happen, which is very exciting, because our listeners will know, you'll know when you're listening to this,
sentences.zh: 而且我们不知道会发生什么，这非常令人兴奋，因为我们的听众会知道，当你听到这里时你就会知道，

sentences.en: but we don't know whether there'll be a deal, whether Britain will have forged manfully into its new future, or whether we'll be, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我们不知道是否会达成协议，英国是会意气风发地迈向它的新未来，还是我们会，你知道的，

sentences.en: blocked up with lorries on the roads and disaster and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 被堵在路上的货车、灾难以及诸如此类的事情所困扰。

sentences.en: So, there's an element of sort of jeopardy, isn't there, Tom?
sentences.zh: 所以，这里面有一种类似高风险的刺激感，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: Very exciting.
sentences.zh: 非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Very, very exciting indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实非常、非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: And I think it's been heroic of us so far in the episodes we've done, barely to mention Brexit.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，我们在之前做过的几期节目中几乎没有提及脱欧，这已经相当英勇了。

sentences.en: Because, I guess, in a way, the arguments about it, whether you are in favour of leaving or remaining, was always about history.
sentences.zh: 因为我猜，从某种程度上讲，关于脱欧的争论——无论你支持离开还是留欧——一直都与历史有关。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're right.
sentences.zh: 是的，你说得对。

sentences.en: They have always been about history.
sentences.zh: 它们一直都与历史有关。

sentences.en: So, that is what we thought we might focus on today, is the comparisons that people have made in the debates over the past few years,
sentences.zh: 所以，这正是我们今天想要聚焦的内容，即人们在过去几年的辩论中所做的种种对比，

sentences.en: between the Brexit that we're going through now, and previous examples of Brexit.
sentences.zh: 在我们正在经历的这次脱欧与以往的脱欧范例之间。

sentences.en: Brexit.
sentences.zh: 脱欧。

sentences.en: And so, well, before we do that, we should quickly say, before you all turn off, we are not going to have any degree of argument about,
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，在此之前，我们应该赶紧声明，免得你们都转台不听了——我们绝不会就

sentences.en: or discussion about whether Brexit was a good thing or a bad thing, or why we did it, or anything like that, are we?
sentences.zh: 脱欧究竟是好事还是坏事、我们为什么要这么做，或者诸如此类的问题展开任何程度的争论或讨论，对吧？

sentences.en: We're going to steer well clear of that, and we're going to wear our historian's hats very firmly.
sentences.zh: 我们要远远避开这些话题，而且我们要牢牢戴紧历史学家的帽子。

sentences.en: I actually suspect we don't really disagree about Brexit, so it wouldn't even be a very interesting podcast anyway.
sentences.zh: 其实我猜我们对脱欧并没有真正的分歧，所以这甚至不会是一个多有趣的播客。

sentences.en: However, we're going to talk about all these fascinating historical comparisons.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们要谈谈所有这些迷人的历史对比。

sentences.en: And do you want to go first, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你想先来吗？

sentences.en: I think you've got a colossal list of possible parallels.
sentences.zh: 我想你有一大长串可能的相似之处。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I've drawn up what I think of the top ten comparisons that people have made.
sentences.zh: 所以，我总结了我认为人们做出的十大对比。

sentences.en: Top ten Brexits.
sentences.zh: 脱欧大盘点前十名。

sentences.en: Top ten Brexits.
sentences.zh: 脱欧大盘点前十名。

sentences.en: Over the centuries, and not just the centuries, over the millennia, because the very first Brexit is the drowning of Doggerland beneath the tsunami, which happened 8,200 years ago.
sentences.zh: 跨越几个世纪，不仅仅是几个世纪，而是跨越几千年，因为最初的脱欧其实是海啸淹没多格尔兰，那发生在8200年前。

sentences.en: And Doggerland, of course, Britain was originally attached to the continent with the ending of the Ice Age.
sentences.zh: 说到多格尔兰，随着冰河时代的结束，英国最初其实是与欧洲大陆相连的。

sentences.en: Enormous amounts of ice get released into the sea, so the sea levels rise, and so this is the results in the North Sea.
sentences.zh: 大量的冰块融化流入海洋，导致海平面上升，这就形成了现在的北海。

sentences.en: And there seems to have been a particular kind of disaster when there were kind of landslips by Norway.
sentences.zh: 而且当时似乎发生了一种特殊类型的灾难，挪威那边发生了一些山体滑坡。

sentences.en: Great tsunami burst across and leaves Britain an island.
sentences.zh: 巨大的海啸呼啸而过，将英国变成了一个岛屿。

sentences.en: And I guess that that is a fairly fundamental event, because the fact that Britain is an island means that geography kind of underpins pretty much everything.
sentences.zh: 我想这是一个相当根本性的事件，因为英国是一个岛屿这一事实意味着地理差不多是一切的基础。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And are you one of these people who thinks that Britain's island nation identity is sort of fundamental to Britishness?
sentences.zh: 你是不是那种认为英国的岛国身份对英国人特质至关重要的人？

sentences.en: Do you think that?
sentences.zh: 你是这么认为的吗？

sentences.en: Do you buy all that?
sentences.zh: 你买账吗？

sentences.en: I do think that the consciousness that we're separated from the mainland of Europe by that narrow strip of water is fairly fundamental.
sentences.zh: 我的确认为，我们通过那片狭窄的水域与欧洲大陆隔离开来的这种意识是相当根本的。

sentences.en: And I think that it generates exactly what we're talking about over this episode, which is this sense of push-me-pull-you,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为它正是我们这期节目所要讨论的内容的根源，也就是这种拉锯感，

sentences.en: that we can't separate ourselves completely from the continent because we're too close to it.
sentences.zh: 我们无法将自己与欧洲大陆完全割裂，因为我们离得太近了。

sentences.en: But equally, the impulse to do that is always there.
sentences.zh: 但同样，这样做的冲动也一直都在。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that that is why we've had all these Brexits.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是为什么我们经历了所有这些脱欧。

sentences.en: Can I ask you a question that shows my ignorance, just about the Doggerland question?
sentences.zh: 我能问你一个暴露出我无知的问题吗，就关于多格尔兰的问题？

sentences.en: When did human beings come to Britain?
sentences.zh: 人类是什么时候来到英国的？

sentences.en: Well, they came in waves, and then the Ice Ages come and crunch and crash everything up, and they retreat, and then they come back.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们是一波一波来的，然后冰河时代到来，把一切都挤压摧毁，他们撤退，然后又卷土重来。

sentences.en: So there were people there who were detached from, you know, who were Brexiteers, involuntary Brexiteers.
sentences.zh: 所以那里曾有脱离于，你知道的，也就是脱欧派，非自愿的脱欧派。

sentences.en: Well, Brexiteers, to the extent that they exit Britain, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就他们脱离英国而言，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there are kind of various hominids who settle in Britain and then retreat when the ice comes down, and then they come back.
sentences.zh: 所以有各种人族在英国定居，然后在冰川南下时撤退，接着又回来了。

sentences.en: But basically, people have been continuously in Britain since the Mesolithic.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，自中石器时代以来，英国就一直有人类连续居住。

sentences.en: So they arrived in Britain, the original inhabitants, because there was this land bridge.
sentences.zh: 所以他们来到英国，作为最初的居民，因为当时有这样一座陆桥。

sentences.en: And interestingly, there was a kind of report early December that said that this Brexit, the Doggerland Brexit,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，12月初左右有一篇报道说，这次脱欧——也就是多格尔兰脱欧，

sentences.en: may actually have been kind of slightly more efter than we'd imagined.
sentences.zh: 实际上可能比我们想象的要稍微温和一点。

sentences.en: Because they're arguing that...
sentences.zh: 因为他们争论说……

sentences.en: Still in the single market.
sentences.zh: 依然留在单一市场里。

sentences.en: Yes, that there were kind of little islands that were left, and that they only gradually sank.
sentences.zh: 是的，当时还残留着一些小岛，而且它们只是逐渐沉没。

sentences.en: So it was a slightly more protracted Brexit.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一次稍微有些拖延的脱欧。

sentences.en: It wasn't quite as hard a Brexit as people had assumed.
sentences.zh: 它不像人们想象的那么彻底。

sentences.en: Anyway, well done.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，干得好。

sentences.en: We've done Doggerland without making the obvious joke, so that's excellent.
sentences.zh: 我们讲完了多格尔兰却没有开那个显而易见的玩笑，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Well done.
sentences.zh: 干得漂亮。

sentences.en: And number two, Dominic, what have you got for us?
sentences.zh: 那么第二点，多米尼克，你给我们准备了什么？

sentences.en: So number two, a few people brought this up.
sentences.zh: 第二点，有几个人提到了这个。

sentences.en: So they asked about Rome.
sentences.zh: 他们问到了罗马。

sentences.en: So Olly Simpson, for example, raised, said AC Grayling had recently compared the EU with the Roman Empire, safety in numbers, quality roads, etc.
sentences.zh: 比如奥利·辛普森就提出，A·C·格雷林最近把欧盟比作罗马帝国，人多安全、道路优质等等。

sentences.en: Apparently it's a bid to make us want to be part of it, says Olly Simpson.
sentences.zh: 奥利·辛普森说，这显然是为了让我们想要成为其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Now, yeah, this is an interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 现在，是的，这是一件很有意思的事情。

sentences.en: So this isn't really us leaving them so much as them leaving us, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这其实不是我们离开他们，更像是他们离开我们，对吧？

sentences.en: That the Romans, well, in the sort of children's history book version of our past, the Romans all leave Britain in what?
sentences.zh: 罗马人——好吧，在我们儿童历史书版本的过去里——罗马人在什么时候全部离开了英国？

sentences.en: Is it 410, right about 410 they're meant to have left?
sentences.zh: 是410年吗？他们大概是在410年离开的吧？

sentences.en: Well, there are two iterations of this, because we also have Andrew Sheldon comments, just Carousius.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有两种说法，因为安德鲁·谢尔顿也提到了卡劳修斯。

sentences.en: And Carousius was a Roman general who had control of the fleet in the Channel, and he essentially grabs hold of Britain and a chunk of northern Gaul and declares his independence.
sentences.zh: 卡劳修斯是一位罗马将军，掌握着海峡舰队，他基本上夺取了英国和北高卢的一部分，并宣布独立。

sentences.en: And this has often been compared to Brexit.
sentences.zh: 这经常被拿来与脱欧作比较。

sentences.en: But actually, Carousius didn't want to leave the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，卡劳修斯并不想离开罗马帝国。

sentences.en: He essentially wanted to be Roman Emperor himself.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是想自己当罗马皇帝。

sentences.en: So I don't think that counts.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这不算数。

sentences.en: So we're not including that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不把这个算进去。

sentences.en: Actually, the Britons do leave.
sentences.zh: 事实上，不列颠人确实离开了。

sentences.en: As far as we can tell, they do actively do a Brexit.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，他们确实实实在在地搞了一次脱欧。

sentences.en: No, the Britons leave.
sentences.zh: 不，不列颠人离开了。

sentences.en: So either 409, 410, as is typical with ancient history, we can't absolutely pin this down.
sentences.zh: 所以无论是在409年还是410年，正如古代历史的常态一样，我们无法完全确定具体时间。

sentences.en: A contemporary historian says that the Britons defected from Roman rule and lived their own lives independent from Roman laws.
sentences.zh: 一位当代历史学家说，不列颠人背叛了罗马统治，过上了独立于罗马法律的生活。

sentences.en: So that does sound like a kind of Brexit.
sentences.zh: 听起来确实像是一种脱欧。

sentences.en: Steve Baker's fantasy.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·贝克的白日梦。

sentences.en: They then seem to have slightly repented it.
sentences.zh: 他们后来似乎有点后悔了。

sentences.en: Again, there are confusions around the sources, but it does seem the Britons write to the Emperor and say, whoa, everything's going wrong.
sentences.zh: 同样，史料记载也有些混乱，但看起来不列颠人确实写信给皇帝说，哇，一切都出乱子了。

sentences.en: Please, can we come back here?
sentences.zh: 求求你，我们能回去吗？

sentences.en: By this point, the Empire's kind of imploding.
sentences.zh: 到了这个时候，帝国已经处於瓦解的边缘了。

sentences.en: And so the Emperor writes back and says, you're on your own.
sentences.zh: 于是皇帝回信说，你们只能靠自己了。

sentences.en: You've got to cope.
sentences.zh: 你们必须自己应付。

sentences.en: And everything goes, it has to be said, that this Brexit in the 5th century doesn't entirely go according to plan.
sentences.zh: 不得不说，5世纪的这次脱欧并没有完全按计划进行。

sentences.en: Because basically, the entire economy in plays.
sentences.zh: 因为基本上，整个经济都崩溃了。

sentences.en: Because the Roman Empire was what enabled the British economy to function.
sentences.zh: 因为罗马帝国才是不列颠经济得以运转的保障。

sentences.en: But this isn't a Brexit as in Britain taking a unique path, though, is it?
sentences.zh: 但这并不是那种英国选择独特道路意义上的脱欧，对吧？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, what happened to Britain at the end of this period, in sort of late antiquity,
sentences.zh: 因为，我是说，在这个时期结束时，在古代晚期左右，英国发生的事情，

sentences.en: is surely exactly what happened to Spain or, you know, Gaul or any of the other kind of provinces of the Western Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 不正是西班牙、高卢或西罗马帝国的任何其他省份所发生的事情吗？

sentences.en: That they fragment.
sentences.zh: 它们解体了。

sentences.en: And even if we wanted to stay in the Roman Empire, there was no Roman Empire in the West anymore to be part of, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，即使我们想留在罗马帝国里，西方也已经没有罗马帝国可供加入了，对吧？

sentences.en: I think that's kind of true.
sentences.zh: 我想这倒也对。

sentences.en: But this happened, you know, the process of Rome's fall happens over several decades across the course of the 10th century.
sentences.zh: 但这发生在，你知道的，罗马灭亡的过程在10世纪的几十里间跨越了多个年代。

sentences.en: This is pretty early.
sentences.zh: 这相当早。

sentences.en: And what is distinctive about it is that the, you know, as the historian says, that the Britons take a decision to cast off Roman laws, Roman rule.
sentences.zh: 而它的独特之处在于，正如历史学家所说，不列颠人做出了抛弃罗马法律和罗马统治的决定。

sentences.en: And I guess Roman tax collectors, that's the kind of the key, the key fact.
sentences.zh: 我想还有罗马收税官，这是个关键事实。

sentences.en: But by casting off the Roman tax collectors, they're also casting off the ability to have a monetary economy.
sentences.zh: 但通过赶走罗马收税官，他们也丢掉了维持货币经济的能力。

sentences.en: And essentially, coinage vanishes for 100, 200 years, 300 years.
sentences.zh: 基本上，铸币消失了100年、200年、300年。

sentences.en: And it's back to barter.
sentences.zh: 一切回到了以物易物的时代。

sentences.en: And that is kind of, you know, that is the Remainer's worst nightmare for what might happen to Brexit Britain, is that we all sit around bartering turnips and things.
sentences.zh: 这有点像，你知道的，留欧派对脱欧英国最可怕的噩梦，就是我们都坐在一起用芜菁之类的事物进行物物交换。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so I think that's quite an interesting one.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: Well, here's a quick question for you before we move on.
sentences.zh: 好了，在我们继续之前，有个小问题问你。

sentences.en: I think the end of Roman Britain is such a fascinating subject.
sentences.zh: 我认为罗马不列颠的结束是一个非常迷人的主题。

sentences.en: We should do a whole podcast on it.
sentences.zh: 我们应该专门做一期播客来聊聊它。

sentences.en: But do people have at that stage any sense of British distinctiveness?
sentences.zh: 但在这个阶段，人们对英国的独特性有什么概念吗？

sentences.en: Surely they don't.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定没有吧。

sentences.en: They don't feel that they are unique and they are separate from other provinces of the Roman Empire in a way that is not true in Spain or in Portugal or wherever.
sentences.zh: 他们不觉得自己在西班牙、葡萄牙或其他地方所不具备的那种方式下是独一无二的，并且与罗马帝国的其他行省分离开来。

sentences.en: Well, it's really hard to know because we have so few, we have almost nothing written by Britons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的很难知道，因为我们的资料太少了，几乎没有什么是不列颠人自己写的。

sentences.en: And I think that one of the things that is distinctive about Britain, for instance, Britain is there are no British senators.
sentences.zh: 我认为英国的独特之处之一在于，例如，英国没有英国参议员。

sentences.en: And you have Gauls who laugh.
sentences.zh: 而你有高卢人，他们会笑。

sentences.en: There is a British poet and a Gaulish poet laughs at the very idea of this.
sentences.zh: 有一位不列颠诗人和一位高卢诗人，高卢诗人对这种想法大加嘲笑。

sentences.en: So you clearly have the sense, even, you know, 4th, 5th centuries, that the Britons are bumpkins, are barbarians, are backward.
sentences.zh: 所以你显然有一种感觉，甚至在4、5世纪时，不列颠人就被视为乡巴佬、野蛮人和落后的人。

sentences.en: And I think one of the measures of what makes Britain distinctive in the Roman Empire and the way that it leaves the Roman Empire is that in Britain we do not speak a form of Latin.
sentences.zh: 我认为衡量英国在罗马帝国中的独特性以及它离开罗马帝国方式的一个标准是，在英国我们不说某种形式的拉丁语。

sentences.en: You do in Spain, you do in Italy, you do in France.
sentences.zh: 你在西班牙说，你在意大利说，你在法国说。

sentences.en: In Britain here we speak a Germanic language.
sentences.zh: 而在英国这里，我们说的是日耳曼语。

sentences.en: And so clearly something,
sentences.zh: 所以显然有些东西，

sentences.en: whether it's something about the relationship of Britain as a province to the rest of the empire or whether it's about the distinctive circumstances in which Britain ceases to be Roman.
sentences.zh: 无论是关于英国作为一个省份与帝国其余部分的关系，还是关于英国不再属于罗马的独特环境。

sentences.en: But clearly the fact that we do not speak a form of Latin, I think, is the measure of just how seismic that Brexit was.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，我们不说某种形式的拉丁语这一事实，我认为就是那次脱欧具有多么震撼性影响的明证。

sentences.en: So I think that's a good one.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: So let's put that right down.
sentences.zh: 那我们就把它记下来。

sentences.en: That's definitely, yeah, that's a tick, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这绝对，是的，这算是一个打勾通过的选项，对吧？

sentences.en: And you were definitely setting yourself at odds with the major powers on the continent.
sentences.zh: 而且你绝对把自己置于与大陆主要大国对立的境地。

sentences.en: So I think that, yeah, I think that's probably the least tendentious parallel of the lot.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，是的，我认为这可能是所有类比中最不具倾向性一个了。

sentences.en: You see, if I was picking, I mean, it's not a very successful parallel, as we've said, but in terms of mattering, I think Dunkirk and the Second World War, I think you get,
sentences.zh: 你看，如果由我来选，我的意思是，正如我们所说，这不是一个很成功的类比，但就重要性而言，我认为敦刻尔克和第二次世界大战，你会发现，

sentences.en: you know, without the Second World War, you don't get Brexit.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，没有二战，就没有脱欧。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously you don't, because the history is different.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然不会有，因为历史不同了。

sentences.en: But the Second World War place, that sort of dad's army, Dan Buster's view of Britain and indeed of Europe is so huge in people's sense of their own national identity.
sentences.zh: 但二战的地位，那种老兵新传、杰出的防空英雄视角对英国乃至欧洲的国民身份认同影响太大了。

sentences.en: And I think it matters so much that Britain is the one major European country that goes through both world wars without being occupied and without being defeated.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，英国是唯一一个经历两次世界大战而没有被占领、也没有被击败的主要欧洲国家，这一点极其重要。

sentences.en: And it means the way we tell the story of the 20th century in which the EU is created is very different from how every other European country tells that story.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们讲述20世纪历史的方式——欧盟正是在这期间诞生的——与欧洲其他国家讲述这段历史的方式截然不同。

sentences.en: Don't you think Dunkirk matters?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得敦刻尔克很重要吗？

sentences.en: OK, if we, based on the fact that we're talking about the most interesting mirror, I will, I'll grant you that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果我们基于我们正在讨论的是最有趣的镜像这一事实，我承认这一点。

sentences.en: I do think it's played a crucial role in...
sentences.zh: 我确实认为它在……中扮演了至关重要的角色。

sentences.en: Are you gutted we didn't choose King John?
sentences.zh: 我们没有选择约翰王，你是不是很沮丧？

sentences.en: Quite disappointed.
sentences.zh: 相当失望。

sentences.en: Yeah, quite disappointed.
sentences.zh: 对，相当失望。

sentences.en: Well, you see, there are a number on these that, if you're expecting the worst, and to reiterate, we don't know whether people, even as we speak,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，这里有几个，如果你对最坏情况有所预期的话，而且再次重申，我们不知道人们，甚至在我们说话的时候，

sentences.en: are squabbling over turnips out on the streets.
sentences.zh: 是否正在街头为抢夺芜菁而争吵。

sentences.en: Quite.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So if that's the case, if there has been no deal and it's all gone disastrously wrong and planes are dropping from the air, then the Roman Brexit, that might be a good comparison.
sentences.zh: 所以如果真是这样，如果达成无协议脱欧，一切都错得一塌糊涂，飞机从空中掉下来，那么罗马脱欧可能是一个很好的比较。

sentences.en: And the John one would be interesting in terms of, you know, if it goes spectacularly wrong, will we perhaps have to go back cap in hand?
sentences.zh: 而约翰王那个在某种意义上也很有趣，就是说，如果事情错得离谱，我们是否可能不得不卑躬屈膝地回去？

sentences.en: The Irish one, I think, is also interesting that even if that happens, probably not.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰那个，我也觉得很有趣，即使那样发生了，可能也不会。

sentences.en: Let me ask you a question, Tom, about the Roman Brexit, which I find so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我想问你一个关于罗马脱欧的问题，我觉得这太迷人了。

sentences.en: When the Romans left, I mean, did they leave?
sentences.zh: 当罗马人离开时，我的意思是，他们真的离开了吗？

sentences.en: Did people...
sentences.zh: 人们……

sentences.en: Who left?
sentences.zh: 谁离开了？

sentences.en: Surely, I mean, the number of people who actually physically left must have been pretty small.
sentences.zh: 当然，我的意思是，真正实体离开的人数一定相当少。

sentences.en: Well, essentially what happens is that Britain has a large number of military forces in it,
sentences.zh: 嗯，本质上发生的情况是，英国驻扎了大量的军事力量，

sentences.en: because there are enemies, North Asians were all in Ireland, increasingly coming across the North Sea.
sentences.zh: 因为有敌人，北方的爱尔兰人都在爱尔兰，而且越来越多地横渡北海。

sentences.en: So there are large quantities of forces in Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以英国有大量的驻军。

sentences.en: And as the centre implodes on the continent, so it becomes incredibly appealing for Roman commanders in Britain to have a crack at becoming emperor.
sentences.zh: 随着大陆中央政权的崩溃，在英国的罗马指挥官们去尝试争当皇帝变得极其具有吸引力。

sentences.en: And so they increasingly strip the province of its garrisons, take them across the channel.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们不断抽调该省的卫戍部队，把他们带过海峡。

sentences.en: They invariably lose.
sentences.zh: 他们无一例外地失败了。

sentences.en: So ultimately what's happened by the beginning of the 5th century is that you no longer have any garrisons, really.
sentences.zh: 所以最终到5世纪初发生的事情是，你基本上不再拥有任何卫戍部队了。

sentences.en: You don't really have any Roman forces left, and yet the Britons are still being required to pay the taxes.
sentences.zh: 你真的不再有任何罗马军队留下来了，然而不列颠人仍然被要求纳税。

sentences.en: So I think that that's essentially what precipitates the kind of, you know, we're Brexiting.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这本质上催生了那种，你知道的，我们要脱欧了的心态。

sentences.en: Their EU budget contributions are not seeing a decent return.
sentences.zh: 他们对欧盟预算的贡献没有看到像样的回报。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly so.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, yeah, interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，很有趣。

sentences.en: But I totally agree about you that we must do a podcast on the end of Roman Britain.
sentences.zh: 但我完全同意你的看法，我们必须做一期关于罗马不列颠终结的播客。

sentences.en: I think it would be very, very interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那会非常非常有趣。

sentences.en: One of our New Year's resolutions.
sentences.zh: 我们新年决心之一。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Anyway, so I hope you've enjoyed that.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，希望你们喜欢这期节目。

sentences.en: Wishing you a very happy New Year and as good a Brexit as we can hope.
sentences.zh: 祝大家新年快乐，也祝我们能迎来一个尽可能好的脱欧。

sentences.en: And I hope everything in 2021 is better than it's been in 2020.
sentences.zh: 希望2021年的每一件事都比2020年更好。

sentences.en: Thanks very much for listening.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢收听。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余烬》。

sentences.zh: 若想收听额外单集、提前解锁、无广告收听以及加入我们的聊天社区，请登录 restishistorypod.com 注册。
